newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: New Afghan rulers seek world recognition.
newsitem.headline: New Afghan rulers seek world recognition.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia appealed on Friday for international recognition of its government after its forces captured the capital Kabul.
"We have captured Kabul and we rule over the major part of Afghanistan," a Taleban spokesman in the southern Afghan town of Kandahar told Reuters by telephone.
"We call upon the international community to recognise us as the government of the Islamic state of Afghanistan," spokesman Wakil Ahmad said.
He said the immediate tasks before the Taleban administration would be enforcement of Islamic Sharia law, restoration of peace in the war-shattered country, and the disarmament of the Afghan people.

Wakil described ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani, Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar and their top military commander Ahmad Shah Masood as "national criminals" for not accepting a Taleban amnesty in return for a surrender. The men fled Kabul before the Taleban marched in.
"They should be handed over to Taleban by whoever gets hold of them," he said.

The Taleban militia's top leader in Kabul, Mullah Mohammad Rabbani, said earler on Friday that those government leaders who fled Kabul before the takeover would be judged according to Islam if they were caught.
He said the men were believed to have fled to Jabal us-Sharaj, the headquarters of military chief Masood at the entrance to the Panjshir valley, or to the valley itself.
"The message is very clear. Anyone who works against Islam will meet the same fate. Anyone who serves Islam can live peacefully," he said.
